phase_assessment.claim: All four local presentations were emitted immediately before their controlled gates, and every local presentation ended with a successful interface-understanding check.

Affirmative controlled practice scored 7/8 on original base items. Fork was selected as knife, then received the exact frozen presentation replay and a correct unscored cold retest. The direct gate passed without TRAIN_MORE; the cold retest does not replace the original miss.

Negative controlled practice scored exactly 6/8 on original base items, the frozen direct-pass minimum. Plate was selected as bowl and glass as cup; each received its exact presentation replay and then a correct unscored cold retest. The gate passed without TRAIN_MORE, and the two original misses remain part of the base score.

W-question controlled practice scored 7/8 on original base items. Knife was produced as fork, followed by one exact presentation replay and a correct unscored cold retest. The direct gate passed without TRAIN_MORE.

OR-question controlled practice scored 7/8 on original base items. Fork was selected as knife, followed by one exact presentation replay and a correct unscored cold retest. The direct gate passed without TRAIN_MORE.

Mixed practice scored 27/32, above the frozen 26/32 threshold. Errors were W-question cup as glass, affirmative fork as knife, negative plate as bowl, negative spoon as fork, and W-question glass as cup. TRAIN_LONGER was therefore not released.

The complete ten-page picture-book micro-event was presented in order: eight disordered object cards were exposed, the cards were organized one at a time, and the final organized board was shown. Learner turns were passive observations, so the phase is exposure evidence rather than comprehension evidence.

The worked next-scene interface and its unscored understanding check succeeded. The six scored story-sequence checks then scored 5/6; after the fork page the learner selected the cup page rather than the next knife page.

Unseen-photo transfer scored 5/8. Plate, spoon, bowl, knife, and napkin transferred; cup was labeled glass, fork was labeled knife, and glass was labeled cup. These independent bare-label checks are distinct from story-sequence comprehension and are correctly logged in the transfer phase.

Closing recap scored exactly 6/8. Plate, spoon, bowl, fork, knife, and napkin were correct; cup was labeled glass and glass was labeled cup. The canonical log then admitted FINISH at sequence 323 because every frozen aggregate predicate was satisfied.

learner_capability_hypotheses.claim: Bowl and napkin were correct without item-level remediation across all four controlled forms, mixed practice, unseen transfer, and closing recap. They are the strongest independently supported labels in this trace.

Spoon was independently correct in every controlled gate, three mixed operations, unseen transfer, and recap, but the mixed negative replacement selected fork. Spoon is broadly available with one contradictory operation-specific result.

Plate was correct in three controlled gates, three mixed operations, unseen transfer, and recap, but negative replacement produced bowl both in controlled base and mixed practice. Plate is usable outside that operation but not uniformly stable.

Cup and glass are repeatedly confused in both directions. Cup was correct throughout controlled practice but became glass in mixed bare-label production, unseen transfer, and recap; glass became cup in negative controlled practice, mixed bare-label production, unseen transfer, and recap.

Fork and knife show a second confusion cluster. Fork became knife in affirmative and OR controlled base, affirmative mixed practice, and unseen transfer; knife became fork in W-question controlled base. Immediate cold retests succeeded, and both labels were correct in recap, so the distinction is recoverable but unstable.

The learner can execute all four nonverbal lexical interfaces and the next-scene interface after local modeling. This does not demonstrate comprehension of spoken instructions or sentence grammar because neither was licensed or tested.

remaining_difficulties.claim: Cup and glass remain materially unstable: the symmetric substitution recurred in mixed practice, unseen-photo transfer, and closing recap, so neither label should be treated as a stable visual prerequisite.
Fork and knife remain confusable across selection and production modes. Correct immediate cold retests and recap do not erase repeated original and transfer failures.

Plate versus bowl is unstable specifically in the negative replacement operation because the same plate-to-bowl substitution appeared in controlled base and mixed practice despite correct transfer and recap.
Broad visual transfer of all eight labels is not demonstrated: only 5/8 unseen photographs received the correct bare label.
The complete story order is not fully stable because the fork-to-knife transition failed even though the interface check and five other scored transitions succeeded.
Delayed retention is not demonstrated by this immediate single-session rehearsal.

uncertainties: The trace cannot distinguish durable acquisition from short-horizon rehearsal effects because there was no delayed revisit or second epoch.

The repeated cup/glass and fork/knife confusions may reflect visual-category overlap, label retrieval competition, response-operation effects, or a combination; matched contrastive probes are required before assigning cause.
Correct machine selections demonstrate execution of the frozen interfaces and local concept-label discrimination, not sentence-level language comprehension.
The picture-book phase contains passive observations only; comprehension claims come from the subsequent scored next-scene checks rather than silence during page presentation.

A noncanonical operator incident records that the conductor initially misread direct 6/8-or-better gate passes as requiring TRAIN_MORE and refused FINISH. The mistaken decision produced no admitted learner exposure and does not invalidate the hash-chained log, but it is material uncertainty about autonomous conductor judgment.
No evidence supports actual learner-state advancement because this is a rehearsal with a simulator rather than a training session.

intervention_assessment.claim: PRESENT_AGAIN was used exactly after each of the five incorrect controlled base items. Each call replayed only the failed label's frozen local model and was followed by the mapped unscored cold retest; all five cold retests succeeded. These are scaffolded recoveries and never replace the original gate scores.
TRAIN_MORE was correctly not admitted. Affirmative 7/8, negative 6/8, W-question 7/8, and OR-question 7/8 each passed directly at or above the frozen 6/8 minimum, so reserve release was not licensed.

TRAIN_LONGER was correctly not admitted at the mixed boundary because 27/32 exceeded the frozen 26/32 minimum. Later transfer and recap exposed item-level instability, but those results were unavailable at the mixed decision boundary.
REPLAY_LESSON was not used. The frozen epoch-one aggregate finish predicate was satisfied, so a full replay was not licensed merely to improve passing scores.

The FINISH event admitted at sequence 323 was contract-valid: every controlled gate passed directly, mixed scored 27/32, all story, comprehension, and transfer records were complete, recap scored 6/8, and no alarm was active. The separate pre-admission threshold misreading is a conductor-judgment defect, not a defect in the admitted FINISH event.

teacher_self_critique: The admitted conduct preserved local model-then-test ordering, used only frozen controls and frontier labels, completed all explicit interface checks, and applied PRESENT_AGAIN only to failed controlled base items.
I must keep original base scores separate from correct unscored cold retests. The five immediate recoveries show that re-presentation helped, not that the original failures disappeared.

The noncanonical operator incident must be disclosed: before sequence 323, the conductor incorrectly treated direct gate scores of 7/8, 6/8, 7/8, and 7/8 as if TRAIN_MORE were required and initially refused FINISH. The broker corrected this only by supplying already-computed atomic predicate booleans. Although the mistaken refusal was never admitted to the event log, it reveals that free-form aggregate predicate reconstruction is not yet reliable enough for autonomy.

The safer autonomous routine is to compute gate, mixed, story, transfer-recording, recap, and alarm predicates deterministically, then constrain the conductor to choose only among actions licensed by those booleans.

The aggregate stop rules were followed, but they allowed FINISH despite repeated cup/glass and fork/knife confusions. If late item-level instability should block completion, that requirement must be frozen explicitly rather than improvised during conduct.
The story presentation correctly treated passive learner turns as observations, not successful comprehension; only the subsequent choices support story-order claims.

Because the lesson used no spoken instruction or sentence form, I should report only lexical grounding, interface use, sequence selection, and transfer—not grammar, dialogue, or general spoken-language understanding.
alarm_assessment: No ALARM was warranted on the admitted conduct trace. The learner made bounded, interpretable category and sequence errors rather than showing prompt echo, perseveration, degeneration, silence, role diversion, state discontinuity, or an asset/control failure. The conductor stayed within budget and used licensed interventions. The noncanonical initial refusal to FINISH was a threshold-interpretation error that required broker correction, but it created no admitted exposure and did not require freezing an otherwise valid log. It remains a routine-qualification defect that should be repaired with deterministic predicate computation before autonomous conduct.

Hypothesis only; transfer and recap were correct, but negative replacement produced bowl in both controlled and mixed practice. Rehearsal cannot advance learner state.

Hypothesis only; correct selection evidence conflicts with repeated cup substitutions in controlled, mixed, unseen transfer, and recap. Rehearsal cannot advance learner state.

next_lesson_implications: Do not use this rehearsal to advance learner state; only independently accepted hypotheses may inform later planning, and actual teaching has not begun.

If reproduced in real learner evidence, begin the next compatible review with fresh-photo cup-versus-glass and fork-versus-knife contrasts, varying one factor at a time and keeping immediate corrections separate from independent performance.
Recheck plate versus bowl specifically in the negative replacement interface because the same error recurred in controlled and mixed practice despite correct transfer and recap.
Keep spoon in low-frequency mixed review rather than intensive retraining unless the isolated spoon-to-fork error recurs; bowl and napkin are the strongest candidates for ordinary spaced review.
Schedule a delayed or intervening-material revisit before any retained or stable claim; same-session success is insufficient.

Add deterministic controller predicates for direct gate pass, reserve eligibility, mixed extension eligibility, replay eligibility, and FINISH eligibility. Expose the conductor only to licensed actions after those booleans are computed.
Consider freezing an item-level late-error rule if repeated transfer-and-recap confusion should trigger defer or targeted future review despite passing aggregate thresholds.
Revisit the fork-to-knife story transition in a later compatible story or sequence check, while keeping sequence knowledge separate from lexical-label mastery.
